Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-5188", "title": "H1N1 Flu (Swine Flu)", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Swine flu is an infection caused by a virus."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It's named for a virus that pigs can get."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "People do not normally get swine flu, but human infections can and do happen."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "In 2009 a strain of swine flu called H1N1 infected many people around the world."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "The virus is contagious and can spread from human to human."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Symptoms of swine flu in people are similar to the symptoms of regular human flu and include fever, cough, sore throat, body aches, headache, chills and fatigue."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "There are antiviral medicines you can take to prevent or treat swine flu."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "There is a vaccine available to protect against swine flu."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "You can help prevent the spread of germs that cause respiratory illnesses like influenza by: Covering your nose and mouth with a tissue when you cough or sneeze."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Throw the tissue in the trash after you use it."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Washing your hands often with soap and water, especially after you cough or sneeze."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "You can also use alcohol-based hand cleaners."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Avoiding touching your eyes, nose or mouth."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Trying to avoid close contact with sick people."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Staying home from work or school if you are sick."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1359", "title": "Quitting Smoking", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "What are the health risks of smoking tobacco?"}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Quitting smoking is important for your health."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Besides being the leading cause of cancer in the United States, smoking tobacco harms most organs of your body and causes many other health problems."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Tobacco smoke contains many chemicals and can even be harmful even if you don't smoke."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Exposure to secondhand smoke can increase the risk of cancer and other diseases."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "If you're pregnant , it can harm your fetus."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "That's because smoking also causes addiction to nicotine, a stimulant drug in tobacco."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Nicotine addiction makes it harder to stop, but quitting smoking can improve the quality and length of your life."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "What are the benefits of quitting smoking?"}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Tobacco use is the most common preventable cause of death."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "The more years you smoke and the more cigarettes you smoke each day, the higher your risk."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Quitting smoking can help reduce your risk of health problems as well as improve the quality of your life."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Some initial benefits of quitting include: Lower heart rate and blood pressure Less carbon monoxide in the blood (carbon monoxide reduces the blood's ability to carry oxygen) Better circulation Less coughing and wheezing Sense of smell and taste return In the long term, quitting tobacco can help you live a longer life."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Your risk of getting cancer decreases with each year you stay smoke-free."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Common methods used to help quit smoking include: Counseling with a health care provider about your smoking habits, readiness to quit, and setting a quit date."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Smoking aids such as nicotine replacement products or medicines to help reduce nicotine addiction."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "These may not be right for you if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, a teenager, or if you have certain medical issues or take certain medicines."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Smoking reduction by slowly reducing the number of cigarettes per day, or stopping smoking altogether, often called \"cold turkey.\" You may need to try different things, but a mixture of counseling and quit-smoking medicine has been shown to be the best method."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Some people think that switching to e-cigarettes can help to quit smoking, but that has not been proven."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "These battery-operated smoking devices look like cigarettes but work differently."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Researchers still have a lot to learn about the health effects of using e-cigarettes."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "When you stop or cut back on smoking, you may have short-term effects such as irritability, anxiety, moodiness, weight gain, or trouble sleeping."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "You can work with your provider to help reduce these symptoms and find the best way for you to quit."}]}, {"id": "MLP-389", "title": "Sarcoidosis", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Sarcoidosis is a condition in which groups of cells in your immune system form small, red, and swollen (inflamed) lumps."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "But they most commonly affect the lungs and lymph nodes in the chest."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Over time, sarcoidosis can cause permanent scarring of organs."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Your immune system creates inflammation to help defend you against germs and sickness."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "But in sarcoidosis, inflammation goes off track."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "It causes the cells in your immune system to form granulomas."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Studies suggest that this inflammation might be triggered by infections and certain substances in the environment such as insecticides and mold ."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "And your genes may affect how your immune system reacts to a trigger."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Who is more likely to develop sarcoidosis?"}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Anyone can develop sarcoidosis, but you are more likely to have it if you: Are older, especially if you are over age 55 Live or work near insecticides, mold, or other substances that may cause inflammation Have a close relative who has sarcoidosis Take certain medicines, such as some types of HIV medicines and monoclonal antibodies Are of African or Scandinavian descent Are female What are the symptoms of sarcoidosis?"}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Many people who have sarcoidosis have no symptoms, or they may feel unwell but without any obvious symptoms."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "If you have symptoms, you may have some general symptoms."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "And you may have other symptoms, which will depend upon which part of the body is affected."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "The general symptoms can include: Fatigue Weight loss Swollen lymph nodes Depression Fever Night sweats (heavy sweating during sleep) The symptoms of sarcoidosis in the lungs can include: Wheezing Cough Shortness of breath Chest pain The symptoms of sarcoidosis in other parts of the body can include: Larger than normal liver or spleen Jaundice , which can make your eyes or skin yellow Nervous system problems , such as: Headache Dizziness Vision problems Seizures Numbness or tingling Heart palpitations or an irregular heartbeat ( arrhythmia ) Pain and swelling in the joints Skin problems such as rashes and growths under the skin There is also a set of symptoms that are called Lofgren's syndrome ."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Some people have Lofgren's syndrome when they first develop sarcoidosis."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "It usually goes away completely within 2 years."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "The symptoms of Lofgren's syndrome may include: Swollen lymph nodes in your chest, neck, chin, armpits, or groin."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "A rash of small, itchy, or painful bumps called erythema nodosum."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "The rash is most often on your head, neck, or legs."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Blurred vision, eye pain or redness, light sensitivity, or watery eyes."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "What other problems can sarcoidosis cause?"}, {"id": "S021", "text": "If untreated, or if the treatment does not work, sarcoidosis can cause serious health problems called complications."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Possible complications include: Lung problems Heart problems Hormone problems Brain , nerve, or muscle problems Kidney problems Severe organ damage How is sarcoidosis diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S023", "text": "There is no single test that can diagnose sarcoidosis, and its symptoms can be similar to the symptoms of many other conditions."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "To find out if you have sarcoidosis, your health care provider: Will ask about your medical history, including your symptoms, lifestyle, and any other health conditions you may have."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Will do a physical exam, which may include: Checking your temperature Checking to see if your lymph nodes, spleen, or liver are swollen Listening to your chest with a stethoscope as you breathe in and out Looking for rashes or sores on your body, such as scalp and lower legs Will likely order various tests, such as: Chest x-rays A biopsy of the skin, lymph nodes, lungs, or other affected organs Blood tests to check your blood counts , hormone levels, and how well your kidneys are working Other imaging tests If you are diagnosed with sarcoidosis, your provider may order other tests to look at how sarcoidosis is affecting the body."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "What are the treatments for sarcoidosis?"}, {"id": "S027", "text": "The goal of treatment for sarcoidosis is remission, which means you still have the condition, but it does not cause you problems."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "You may not need treatment, and sometimes the condition goes away on its own."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "If you do need treatment, which treatment(s) you get will depend on your symptoms, which organs are affected, and whether those organs are working well."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "You may be given medicines to: Lower inflammation Treat an overactive immune response Treat joint pain Treat skin problems If you have complications from sarcoidosis, you may need other treatments, such as other medicines, surgery, oxygen therapy , pulmonary rehabilitation , or an implanted cardiac pacemaker or defibrillator ."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Whether or not you have symptoms from sarcoidosis, it's important to get regular follow-up care from your provider, make healthy lifestyle changes, and contact your provider if you have any new symptoms."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "NIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1616", "title": "Nutrition for Older Adults", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "What is nutrition and why is it important for older adults?"}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Nutrition is about eating a healthy and balanced diet so your body gets the nutrients that it needs."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Nutrients are substances in foods that our bodies need so they can function and grow."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "They include carbohydrates , fats , proteins , vitamins , minerals , and water."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Good nutrition is important, no matter what your age."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "It gives you energy and can help you control your weight."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "It may also help prevent some diseases, such as osteoporosis , high blood pressure , heart disease , type 2 diabetes , and certain cancers."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "But as you age, your body and life change, and so does what you need to stay healthy."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "For example, you may need fewer calories, but you still need to get enough nutrients."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "What can make it harder for me to eat healthy as I age?"}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Some changes that can happen as you age can make it harder for you to eat healthy."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "These include changes in your: Home life, such as suddenly living alone or having trouble getting around Health, which can make it harder for you to cook or feed yourself Medicines, which can change how food tastes, make your mouth dry, or take away your appetite Income, which means that you may not have as much money for food Sense of smell and taste Problems chewing or swallowing your food How can I eat healthy as I age?"}, {"id": "S012", "text": "To stay healthy as you age, you should: Eat foods that give you lots of nutrients without a lot of extra calories , such as Fruits and vegetables (choose different types with bright colors) Whole grains, like oatmeal, whole-wheat bread, and brown rice Fat-free or low-fat milk and cheese, or soy or rice milk that has added vitamin D and calcium Seafood, lean meats, poultry, and eggs Beans, nuts, and seeds Avoid empty calories."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "These are foods with lots of calories but few nutrients, such as chips, candy, baked goods, soda, and alcohol."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Pick foods that are low in cholesterol and fat."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "You especially want to try to avoid saturated and trans fats."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Saturated fats are usually fats that come from animals."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Trans fats are processed fats in stick margarine and vegetable shortening."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "You may find them in some store-bought baked goods and fried foods at some fast-food restaurants."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Drink enough liquids , so you don't get dehydrated ."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Some people lose their sense of thirst as they age."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "And certain medicines might make it even more important to have plenty of fluids."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "If you have started losing your appetite, exercising may help you to feel hungrier."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "What can I do if I am having trouble eating healthy?"}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Sometimes health issues or other problems can make it hard to eat healthy."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Here are some tips that might help: If you are tired of eating alone, try organizing some potluck meals or cooking with a friend."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "You can also look into having some meals at a nearby senior center, community center, or religious facility."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "If you are having trouble chewing, see your dentist to check for problems If you are having trouble swallowing, try drinking plenty of liquids with your meal."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "If that does not help, check with your health care provider."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "A health condition or medicine could be causing the problem."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "If you're having trouble smelling and tasting your food, try adding color and texture to make your food more interesting If you aren't eating enough, add some healthy snacks throughout the day to help you get more nutrients and calories If an illness is making it harder for you to cook or feed yourself, check with your health care provider."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "He or she may recommend an occupational therapist, who can help you find ways to make it easier."}]}, {"id": "MLP-4596", "title": "Floods", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Weather such as heavy rain, thunderstorms, hurricanes , or tsunamis can cause flooding."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Flooding can also happen when a river or stream overflows its bank, when a levee is breached, or when a dam breaks."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Flash floods, which can develop quickly, often have a dangerous wall of roaring water."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "The wall carries rocks, mud, and rubble and can sweep away most things in its path."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Be aware of flood hazards no matter where you live, but especially if you live in a low-lying area, near water or downstream from a dam."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Although there are no guarantees of safety during a flood, you can take actions to protect yourself."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Being prepared can help reduce fear, anxiety, and losses."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "If you do experience a disaster, it is normal to feel stressed."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "You may need help in finding ways to cope ."}]}]
